criteria.statement: A published opportunity whose proposal deadline has passed closes on its own: it moves to the first evaluation stage of its program, every proposal submitted against it moves to review, and its author is notified that it is ready for evaluation.
criteria.given: a published opportunity whose proposal deadline has passed
criteria.when: the service next handles any request
criteria.then: the opportunity moves to its program's first evaluation stage with the note "This opportunity has closed.", its submitted proposals move to review, and its author receives a notification
notes: closure is driven by ordinary traffic rather than a clock, throttled so it runs at most once a minute, and additionally attached to the health-check route so that it still runs when the site is idle. An opportunity therefore closes at the first request after its deadline, not at the deadline itself.

criteria.statement: An anonymous visitor or a vendor sees only opportunities that have been published; drafts and opportunities under review are not listed to them and cannot be opened by them.
criteria.given: an opportunity in draft or under review
criteria.when: an anonymous visitor or a vendor lists opportunities, or opens that opportunity's address directly
criteria.then: the opportunity does not appear in the list, and opening it directly reports that it was not found

criteria.statement: A member of public sector staff sees every published opportunity plus their own drafts and opportunities under review, and an administrator sees every opportunity.
criteria.given: two members of public sector staff, each with an unpublished opportunity of their own
criteria.when: each lists opportunities
criteria.then: each sees their own unpublished opportunity and not the other's, while an administrator listing opportunities sees both

criteria.statement: Every change to an opportunity's content creates a new version of it and records an edit in its history; the opportunity always shows its most recent version.
criteria.given: a published opportunity
criteria.when: an administrator changes its description and saves
criteria.then: the opportunity shows the new description, its history gains an entry recording that it was edited, by whom and when, and the previous content is retained

criteria.statement: Any signed-in person may watch an opportunity they did not create, may stop watching it, and cannot watch the same opportunity twice.
criteria.given: a signed-in person viewing an opportunity created by somebody else and not yet watched by them
criteria.when: they choose to watch it, and then choose to watch it again
criteria.then: the first request records them as watching it and the second is refused as a duplicate
notes: a person is refused when they try to watch their own opportunity, with the message "You cannot subscribe to your own opportunity."

criteria.statement: Opening an opportunity's public page counts as a view of that opportunity.
criteria.given: an opportunity that has been viewed a known number of times
criteria.when: anyone, signed in or not, opens its public page
criteria.then: the recorded view count for that opportunity increases by one

criteria.statement: Only signed-in public sector staff and administrators may create an opportunity; a request from a vendor or an anonymous visitor is refused.
criteria.given: a visitor who is not signed in, or is signed in as a vendor
criteria.when: they attempt to create an opportunity
criteria.then: the request is refused and no opportunity is created

criteria.statement: Every opportunity belongs to exactly one of three procurement programs — Code With Us, Sprint With Us or Team With Us — chosen when it is created and never changed afterwards.
criteria.given: a member of public sector staff creating a new opportunity
criteria.when: they choose a program and complete creation
criteria.then: the opportunity is filed under that program and offers only that program's fields, stages and actions
notes: the running code implements three programs, but the application's own README describes only Code With Us and Sprint With Us, and its generated database-schema document lists no Team With Us tables at all. Both documents predate Team With Us; a human should confirm that all three programs carry forward rather than assuming the documents are merely stale.

criteria.statement: An opportunity saved as a draft is accepted with incomplete content; when its proposal deadline, assignment date or start date is missing or invalid it is set to fourteen days from the day of saving, and its completion date is left empty.
criteria.given: a member of public sector staff filling in a new opportunity
criteria.when: they save it as a draft with fields still blank
criteria.then: the draft is stored, no content validation error is raised, and absent dates are set to fourteen days from the day of saving

criteria.statement: An opportunity that is not a draft is rejected unless it carries a title of 1 to 200 characters, a teaser of at most 500 characters, a location, and a description of 1 to 10,000 characters.
criteria.given: a member of public sector staff creating or editing an opportunity that is not a draft
criteria.when: they submit it with a missing title, a title over 200 characters, a teaser over 500 characters, a missing location, or a description that is missing or over 10,000 characters
criteria.then: the submission is rejected and the offending field is named in the response

criteria.statement: An opportunity that is not a draft must state whether remote work is acceptable, and must carry a remote-work description of up to 500 characters whenever remote work is acceptable.
criteria.given: a member of public sector staff creating or editing an opportunity that is not a draft
criteria.when: they mark it as accepting remote work but leave the remote-work description empty
criteria.then: the submission is rejected
notes: when remote work is not acceptable the remote-work description may be empty, and any value over 500 characters is rejected either way.

criteria.statement: A Code With Us opportunity must offer a reward of at least $1 and at most $70,000, and must name at least one skill.
criteria.given: a member of public sector staff creating or editing a Code With Us opportunity that is not a draft
criteria.when: they submit a reward outside $1 to $70,000, or submit no skills
criteria.then: the submission is rejected
notes: duplicate skills are silently collapsed rather than rejected.

criteria.statement: A Sprint With Us opportunity must state a total maximum budget of at least $1 and at most $5,000,000, while a Team With Us opportunity must state a maximum budget of at least $1 with no upper limit.
criteria.given: a member of public sector staff creating or editing an opportunity that is not a draft
criteria.when: they submit a Sprint With Us budget above $5,000,000, or any budget below $1
criteria.then: the submission is rejected
notes: the absence of an upper budget limit on Team With Us is a difference from the other two programs, not a stated policy; nothing in the application explains it, so a human should rule on whether it carries forward.

criteria.statement: An opportunity's key dates must run in order — the proposal deadline no earlier than today, then the assignment date, then the start date, then the completion date — and each date is recorded as 4:00 p.m. Pacific time on the day chosen.
criteria.given: a member of public sector staff creating or editing an opportunity that is not a draft
criteria.when: they submit a proposal deadline in the past, or any later date that falls before the date preceding it
criteria.then: the submission is rejected
notes: when an already-published opportunity's deadline has passed, an edit is measured against that past deadline instead of today, so a closed opportunity can be edited without its dates being forced forward.

criteria.statement: A Sprint With Us or Team With Us opportunity is rejected unless its evaluation weights total exactly one hundred per cent.
criteria.given: a member of public sector staff creating or editing a Sprint With Us or Team With Us opportunity that is not a draft
criteria.when: they submit weights that do not total one hundred per cent
criteria.then: the submission is rejected with a message saying the scoring weights must total 100%
notes: Sprint With Us weights four stages (questions, code challenge, team scenario, price); Team With Us weights three (questions, challenge, price). Each individual weight is separately required to fall between 0 and 100.

criteria.statement: A Sprint With Us opportunity must have an implementation phase, and may only have an inception phase if it also has a prototype phase.
criteria.given: a member of public sector staff creating or editing a Sprint With Us opportunity that is not a draft
criteria.when: they include an inception phase but no prototype phase
criteria.then: the submission is rejected with a message saying a prototype phase must follow an inception phase

criteria.statement: Each evaluation question on a Sprint With Us or Team With Us opportunity carries a question, a guideline, a maximum score, a response word limit and a position, and an optional minimum score that must be lower than the question's maximum score.
criteria.given: a member of public sector staff adding an evaluation question to an opportunity
criteria.when: they submit a question or guideline outside 1 to 1,000 characters, a score below 1, a word limit outside 1 to 3,000, a position outside 0 to 100, or a minimum score equal to or above the question's score
criteria.then: the submission is rejected and the offending field is named
notes: the same limits apply to Sprint With Us "team questions" and Team With Us "resource questions"; the two differ only in name.

criteria.statement: Each resource on a Team With Us opportunity names one service area and a target allocation between 1 and 100 per cent of full time.
criteria.given: a member of public sector staff creating or editing a Team With Us opportunity that is not a draft
criteria.when: they submit a resource with a target allocation outside 1 to 100, or a service area that is not one of the five recognised areas
criteria.then: the submission is rejected

criteria.statement: An opportunity moves through the states draft, under review, published, one or more program-specific evaluation stages, processing, and finally awarded or cancelled.
criteria.given: any opportunity
criteria.when: its state is read at any point in its life
criteria.then: the state is one of the values recognised for its program, and no other value is accepted by the store
notes: Code With Us has a single evaluation stage; Sprint With Us has four (team questions individual, team questions consensus, code challenge, team scenario); Team With Us has three (resource questions individual, resource questions consensus, challenge).

criteria.statement: An opportunity may only change state along the permitted path for its program, and a request for any other change is refused.
criteria.given: an opportunity in a given state
criteria.when: someone requests a change to a state that is not reachable from it — for example from draft straight to an evaluation stage, or out of an awarded or cancelled opportunity
criteria.then: the request is refused and the opportunity's state is unchanged
notes: a draft may go to under review or straight to published; under review may only go to published; published and every evaluation stage may go to the next stage or to cancelled; awarded and cancelled are final.

criteria.statement: Submitting a draft opportunity for review is refused unless the opportunity is complete, and the person is told the opportunity is incomplete rather than which field is missing.
criteria.given: a draft opportunity with a field still blank
criteria.when: its author submits it for review
criteria.then: the request is refused with a message saying the opportunity is incomplete and asking the author to complete and save the form
notes: Code With Us checks only title, teaser, remote-work fields, location and description at this point, while Sprint With Us additionally checks budget, skills, weights and every phase — so a Code With Us opportunity can reach "under review" with a missing reward or missing skills and be caught only at publication.

criteria.statement: Only an administrator may publish an opportunity.
criteria.given: an opportunity in draft or under review
criteria.when: a member of public sector staff who is not an administrator asks to publish it
criteria.then: the request is refused and the opportunity stays unpublished

criteria.statement: Publishing an opportunity records the moment of publication, which is thereafter shown as the opportunity's published date.
criteria.given: an opportunity that has been published
criteria.when: anyone views it
criteria.then: the date shown as its publication date is the moment of the first publication, even if it was later republished

criteria.statement: On closing a Sprint With Us or Team With Us opportunity, each submitted proposal is given an anonymous proponent name for use during evaluation.
criteria.given: a published Sprint With Us or Team With Us opportunity with submitted proposals
criteria.when: it closes at its proposal deadline
criteria.then: each submitted proposal is labelled "Proponent 1", "Proponent 2" and so on
notes: Code With Us does not anonymise proponents.

criteria.statement: An opportunity moves to processing on its own once every proposal still in contention has been scored at its program's final evaluation stage.
criteria.given: an opportunity at its final evaluation stage with at least one proposal still in contention
criteria.when: the last of those proposals is scored
criteria.then: the opportunity moves to processing and the change is recorded with a note saying it was moved automatically because all proposals have been evaluated

criteria.statement: Awarding a proposal moves its opportunity to awarded and records the winning proponent against it; every other proposal still in contention is marked not awarded.
criteria.given: an opportunity in processing with proposals against it
criteria.when: an administrator awards one of those proposals
criteria.then: the opportunity moves to awarded, the winning proponent is recorded against it, and the remaining proposals are marked not awarded

criteria.statement: An awarded opportunity shows its successful proponent's name to everyone, and shows the proponent's contact details and score only to those permitted to see the proposal's score.
criteria.given: an awarded opportunity
criteria.when: a visitor who may not see proposal scores views it
criteria.then: the successful proponent's name is shown and their contact details and score are withheld

criteria.statement: Only an administrator may cancel an opportunity, and only once it has been published.
criteria.given: an opportunity that is published or at any evaluation stage or in processing
criteria.when: an administrator cancels it, giving an optional note of up to 1,000 characters
criteria.then: the opportunity moves to cancelled and stops accepting proposals
notes: a draft or under-review opportunity cannot be cancelled — it is deleted instead.

criteria.statement: The names of the people who created and last changed an opportunity are shown only to administrators and to those people themselves.
criteria.given: a published opportunity
criteria.when: it is viewed by someone who is neither an administrator nor the person who created or last changed it
criteria.then: the creating and changing people's names are absent from what is shown

criteria.statement: An opportunity's administrator and its author can see its full change history, how many times it has been viewed, how many people are watching it and how many proposals have been submitted; nobody else can.
criteria.given: a published opportunity that has been viewed, watched and proposed against
criteria.when: its author or an administrator opens it
criteria.then: they see its history of state changes and events and its counts of views, watchers and submitted proposals
notes: the reporting counts are withheld while the opportunity is still a draft or under review, even from the author.

criteria.statement: Public sector staff cannot see the proposals submitted against an opportunity until it has left the published state.
criteria.given: a published opportunity that has received proposals
criteria.when: its author or an administrator asks to see the proposals
criteria.then: the request is refused until the opportunity has closed and moved to an evaluation stage

criteria.statement: An addendum of 1 to 5,000 characters may be added to any opportunity that is no longer a draft, by an administrator or by the staff member who created it, and cannot be removed afterwards.
criteria.given: a published opportunity
criteria.when: its author adds an addendum
criteria.then: the addendum is appended to the opportunity with its author and date, an entry is added to the opportunity's history, and there is no action that removes it

criteria.statement: An administrator or an opportunity's author may attach a private note, with files, to a Code With Us or Sprint With Us opportunity's history at any point in its life.
criteria.given: a Code With Us or Sprint With Us opportunity in any state
criteria.when: its author adds a note of up to 1,000 characters with attachments
criteria.then: the note and its attachments appear in the opportunity's history, which only the author and administrators can see
notes: Team With Us offers no such action at all. Nothing in the application explains the omission, so a human should decide whether it is a gap to close or a deliberate difference.

criteria.statement: Publishing an opportunity notifies everyone who has asked for new-opportunity notifications, and separately confirms the publication to the opportunity's author.
criteria.given: an opportunity ready to be published and people who have turned notifications on
criteria.when: an administrator publishes it
criteria.then: each of those people receives a notice that a new opportunity has been posted, and the opportunity's author receives a confirmation

criteria.statement: Changing or adding an addendum to an opportunity that is neither a draft nor cancelled notifies everyone watching it, everyone who has submitted a proposal to it, and its author.
criteria.given: a published opportunity with watchers and submitted proposals
criteria.when: an administrator edits it or adds an addendum
criteria.then: its watchers, its proponents and its author are each notified once
notes: nobody is notified when the opportunity is a draft or has been cancelled.

criteria.statement: Cancelling an opportunity notifies everyone watching it and everyone who has submitted a proposal to it, and separately notifies its author.
criteria.given: a published opportunity with watchers and submitted proposals
criteria.when: an administrator cancels it
criteria.then: its watchers and proponents are told it has been cancelled, and its author is told separately that the cancellation was actioned

criteria.statement: Submitting an opportunity for review notifies every administrator, and confirms the submission to its author.
criteria.given: a complete draft opportunity
criteria.when: its author submits it for review
criteria.then: every administrator is notified that an opportunity awaits review, and the author receives a confirmation

criteria.statement: The opportunity list groups opportunities into unpublished, open and closed, showing open opportunities with the nearest proposal deadline first, closed ones most recently closed first, and unpublished ones most recently changed first.
criteria.given: a set of opportunities in a mix of states
criteria.when: someone opens the opportunity list
criteria.then: each opportunity appears in exactly one of the three groups, ordered as described
notes: an opportunity counts as open only while it is published and its proposal deadline is still in the future; everything published and past its deadline, including cancelled and awarded opportunities, counts as closed.

criteria.statement: The opportunity list can be narrowed by program, by state, to remote-friendly opportunities only, and by free text matched against title and location.
criteria.given: a list of opportunities across all three programs
criteria.when: someone selects a program, selects a state, ticks remote-only, or types words into the search box
criteria.then: only opportunities matching every chosen condition remain visible
notes: the state filter offers draft, under review, published, evaluation and awarded; there is no option for opportunities in processing or cancelled, so those can only be found by clearing the filter.

criteria.statement: Only an administrator can open the full report of a completed opportunity, which shows the opportunity, its addenda, its history and every proposal in one continuous document.
criteria.given: an opportunity that has been evaluated
criteria.when: a member of public sector staff who is not an administrator opens its report address
criteria.then: they are refused, while an administrator opening the same address sees the whole record in one document

criteria.statement: Advancing a Sprint With Us or Team With Us opportunity out of the consensus stage is refused unless every consensus evaluation has been submitted and at least one proponent has met the minimum score on every question that sets one.
criteria.given: a Sprint With Us or Team With Us opportunity at the questions consensus stage
criteria.when: its author asks to move it on while a consensus is unsubmitted, or while no proponent has cleared every question's minimum score
criteria.then: the request is refused and the reason is named

criteria.statement: Advancing a Sprint With Us opportunity to the team scenario stage is refused unless every proponent in the code challenge has been scored or disqualified and at least one remains screened in.
criteria.given: a Sprint With Us opportunity at the code challenge stage
criteria.when: its author asks to move it to the team scenario stage while a proponent is unscored and not disqualified
criteria.then: the request is refused with a message saying all proponents must be scored first

criteria.statement: The evaluation panel of a Sprint With Us or Team With Us opportunity may be changed only while the opportunity is a draft, under review, published, or at the first questions stage.
criteria.given: a Sprint With Us or Team With Us opportunity that has reached the consensus stage or beyond
criteria.when: its author asks to change the evaluation panel
criteria.then: the request is refused and the panel stays as it was

criteria.statement: A member of public sector staff who is not an administrator can publish a Code With Us opportunity directly, by creating it as published rather than by publishing an existing one.
criteria.given: a member of public sector staff who is not an administrator
criteria.when: they create a Code With Us opportunity with its state set to published
criteria.then: the opportunity is created and published, and the subscriber notifications for a published opportunity are sent
notes: this contradicts the administrator-only publication rule recovered as R-1.22. The equivalent Sprint With Us and Team With Us creation checks refuse this case explicitly, so the Code With Us omission reads as an oversight rather than an intended difference. There is no replacement criterion because the corrected behaviour is already stated by R-1.22; a human should rule on whether the rebuild simply closes the hole.
superseded by R-1.48

criteria.statement: A Team With Us opportunity in processing can be awarded, even though the recorded set of permitted state changes does not include that step.
criteria.given: a Team With Us opportunity in processing
criteria.when: an administrator awards one of its proposals
criteria.then: the opportunity becomes awarded
notes: the permitted-change table for Team With Us allows only cancellation out of processing, while the equivalent tables for the other two programs allow the award. Awarding does not consult that table, so the award succeeds anyway. Whether the table or the award path is wrong cannot be determined from the application; a human should rule.
superseded by R-1.49

criteria.statement: A Sprint With Us or Team With Us opportunity can be moved out of its consensus stage by a second, older action that does not check whether the consensus evaluations have been submitted.
criteria.given: a Sprint With Us opportunity at the questions consensus stage with consensus evaluations still unsubmitted
criteria.when: its author uses the older "start code challenge" action rather than the newer "finalize consensuses" action
criteria.then: the opportunity advances to the code challenge stage without the consensus check being applied
notes: the application marks the Sprint With Us version of this action as deprecated in a comment but still accepts it; the Team With Us equivalent carries no such comment. There is no replacement criterion because the intended guard is already stated by R-1.41; a human should rule on removing the older path.
superseded by R-1.50

criteria.statement: "Suspended" remains a permitted stored state for an opportunity although no action can put an opportunity into it.
criteria.given: the set of states an opportunity may hold
criteria.when: any state change is attempted
criteria.then: no path leads to the suspended state, and no listing, filter or transition treats it as reachable
notes: the state is named "deprecated suspended" in the application's own code but is still accepted by the store's constraint, so historical records may hold it. There is no replacement criterion: whether the rebuild must still display an opportunity left in this state from the old data is a question for a human, not something the application answers.
superseded by R-1.51

criteria.statement: Creating an opportunity with its state set to published is refused unless the requester is an administrator; a public sector employee who is not an administrator may create an opportunity only as a draft or under review, in all three programs.
The permitted state changes for a Team With Us opportunity in processing are awarded and cancelled, matching Code With Us and Sprint With Us, so the recorded transitions and the award path agree.

There is exactly one path out of a questions consensus stage, and it refuses to advance unless every consensus evaluation has been submitted and at least one proponent has met the minimum score on every question that sets one.

The application's published interface description for opportunities is incomplete: it omits the Team With Us program entirely, omits the "submit for review" and "add note" actions, and describes only two of the three states an opportunity may be created in.
criteria.given: someone reading the application's own interface description to learn what an opportunity supports
criteria.when: they compare it against what the service actually accepts
criteria.then: they find actions and states the description does not mention, and no description at all for one of the three programs
notes: recorded so that the gap is not mistaken for absent behaviour by a later reader. The behaviours themselves are stated in the criteria above; this criterion is about the documentation being an unreliable second source, which is why several criteria here are graded on code alone.

It records that the old application's own interface description is incomplete, which is a property of the recovered sources rather than a behaviour the rebuilt system must exhibit; the behaviours it points at are already carried by the criteria above, and the documentation's unreliability belongs in the archaeology journal.

criteria.statement: The rebuilt system defines no suspended state for an opportunity: none can be created in it, moved to it or stored in it, and any historical record carrying it is mapped to a defined state before the rebuilt system reads it.
A Sprint With Us or Team With Us opportunity must name an evaluation panel of at least two distinct public sector employees, with at most one of them marked as chair.
criteria.given: a member of public sector staff creating or editing a Sprint With Us or Team With Us opportunity
criteria.when: they submit fewer than two panel members, the same person twice, more than one chair, or anyone who is not a public sector employee
criteria.then: the submission is rejected and the reason is named
notes: the rule as written in the application's own comment says "one and only one chair", but the code accepts a panel with no chair at all and rejects only a second chair. A human should rule on which was intended.
Must a Sprint With Us or Team With Us evaluation panel have exactly one chair, as the application's own comment states, or is a chair optional, as the code allows?
superseded by R-1.55

criteria.statement: An opportunity may be deleted only while it is a draft or under review: an administrator may delete one in either state, and the public sector employee who created it may delete it only while it is a draft. The same rule governs Code With Us, Sprint With Us and Team With Us alike, and any other request to delete is refused and the opportunity remains.
criteria.given: an opportunity that has been published at any point
criteria.when: anyone asks to delete it
criteria.then: the request is refused and the opportunity remains
notes: the application's own interface documentation says deletion is permitted only for a draft, while the code also permits an administrator to delete an opportunity that is under review. The three programs also disagree with each other: for Code With Us and Sprint With Us the creating staff member may delete only a draft, but for Team With Us they may also delete one that is under review. A human should rule on the intended rule before it is carried forward.

Which single deletion rule carries forward across all three programs: may an administrator delete an opportunity that is under review as well as one in draft, and may the creating public sector employee delete one that is under review, or only a draft?

criteria.statement: The author of a published opportunity, who is not an administrator, can change its details.
criteria.given: a published opportunity created by a member of public sector staff who is not an administrator
criteria.when: that person submits a change to its details
criteria.then: the change is accepted and a new version is recorded
notes: the interface offers the edit only to administrators once an opportunity is published, but the underlying service accepts it from the author too. The two disagree, and nothing in the application says which is intended.
May the author of a published opportunity who is not an administrator change its details, as the service accepts, or is editing after publication administrator-only, as the interface enforces?
superseded by R-1.56

criteria.statement: A Sprint With Us or Team With Us opportunity must name an evaluation panel of at least two distinct public sector employees, exactly one of whom is the chair; a submission with fewer than two members, the same person twice, no chair, more than one chair, or anyone who is not a public sector employee is rejected and the reason is named.

Once an opportunity is published, only an administrator may change its details; a request from the public sector employee who created it is refused, and the same rule governs Code With Us, Sprint With Us and Team With Us alike.
Anyone, signed in or not, can browse the list of registered organizations, which shows only organizations that have not been archived, ordered by legal name and split into pages.
criteria.given: three registered organizations, one of which has been archived
criteria.when: a visitor who is not signed in opens the organization list
criteria.then: the two organizations that are not archived are listed in alphabetical order by legal name, and the archived one is absent
notes: the page requests fifty organizations at a time; asking for a page beyond the last one returns the first page instead of an empty one.

criteria.statement: Only a signed-in vendor who has already accepted the service's terms and conditions may register a new organization; a request from anyone else is refused.
criteria.given: a signed-in member of public sector staff and a signed-in vendor who has accepted the terms
criteria.when: each tries to register an organization
criteria.then: the vendor's organization is created and the public sector staff member's request is refused as not permitted

criteria.statement: An organization's full record can be opened only by an administrator or by a member who owns or administers that organization; anyone else is refused.
criteria.given: an organization with an owner, one administrator and one ordinary member
criteria.when: the ordinary member, and separately a member of public sector staff, opens that organization's management page
criteria.then: both are refused, while the owner, the organization's administrator and a service administrator each see the organization
notes: the ordinary member is shown a "not found" page rather than a refusal, because the front end turns the refused read into a missing page.

criteria.statement: An organization's profile details may be changed only by an administrator or by the organization's owner; an organization administrator who is not the owner cannot save changes to them.
criteria.given: an organization whose owner has granted administrator rights to another member
criteria.when: that organization administrator opens the organization's profile, edits the legal name and saves
criteria.then: the change is refused and an error is shown
notes: the management page offers the Edit and Archive controls to anyone who can open it, including an organization administrator, but the service only accepts profile changes and archiving from the owner or a service administrator, so the controls are visible to a person who cannot use them. No corrected criterion has been written because it is unclear whether the intent is to widen the permission or to hide the controls.
superseded by R-3.18

criteria.statement: A change to an organization's contact phone number made while editing its profile is not saved.
criteria.given: an organization whose owner is editing its profile
criteria.when: they change the contact phone number and save
criteria.then: every other edited field is saved but the contact phone number is not updated
notes: the profile-update request is read field by field, and the contact phone is read from a differently named field than the one the form sends, so the submitted value never reaches the stored record. Whether the stored number is left as it was or cleared could not be settled from the source alone, because it depends on how the database layer treats a value it was not given.
superseded by R-3.19

criteria.statement: An administrator or an organization's owner may archive the organization, after which it no longer appears in the organization list, cannot be used on proposals, and disappears from its members' lists of organizations; the archiving is recorded with the date and the person who did it.
criteria.given: an active organization with an owner and one other active member
criteria.when: the owner archives it
criteria.then: it is gone from the public organization list, gone from the other member's affiliated organizations, and its record carries the date it was archived and the identity of the person who archived it
notes: archiving does not delete the organization or its memberships; the record is retained and simply marked inactive.

criteria.statement: An organization's owner, its administrators and a service administrator may invite people to the team by email address, and each invitation is created as a pending membership.
criteria.given: an organization with an owner and no other members
criteria.when: the owner invites two email addresses at once from the team page
criteria.then: both people appear on the team list marked as pending, and neither counts towards the organization's team size until they accept
notes: an ordinary member of the organization is not permitted to invite anybody.

criteria.statement: A person may only be invited to an organization if they hold an active vendor account, and cannot be invited twice to the same organization.
criteria.given: an organization with one pending invitation outstanding for a given person
criteria.when: the owner invites that same person again, and separately invites a member of public sector staff
criteria.then: the repeat invitation is refused as the person already being a member of the organization, and the invitation to public sector staff is refused because only vendors may be invited
notes: a person whose membership was previously ended can be invited again, because ended memberships are not counted when checking for an existing one; this was read from the shape of the duplicate check rather than observed.

criteria.statement: A pending invitation becomes an active membership only when the invited person accepts it, or when an administrator accepts it on their behalf; nobody else can accept it and an invitation that is not pending cannot be accepted.
criteria.given: a person with a pending invitation to an organization
criteria.when: the organization's owner tries to accept it on their behalf, and then the invited person accepts it themselves
criteria.then: the owner's attempt is refused, the invited person's acceptance makes the membership active, and a further attempt to accept the now-active membership is refused as not pending
notes: the published interface description gives this operation a different request method than the service actually accepts, so the description cannot be followed literally.

criteria.statement: A membership can be ended by the member themselves, by the organization's owner or administrators, or by a service administrator; the membership becomes inactive rather than being erased, and the person stops counting towards the organization's team.
criteria.given: an organization with an owner and one further active member
criteria.when: that member chooses to leave the organization
criteria.then: they no longer appear on the organization's team list, the organization's team size falls to one, and the organization is no longer listed among their affiliated organizations

criteria.statement: An organization's last remaining owner cannot be removed from it.
criteria.given: an organization with exactly one owner and two other active members
criteria.when: an administrator tries to end the owner's membership
criteria.then: the request is refused with a message saying this is the sole owner for the organization, and the membership remains

criteria.statement: An organization's owner, its administrators and a service administrator may grant or withdraw administrator rights over the organization to an active member, but nobody may change their own rights and the owner's own membership cannot be changed this way.
criteria.given: an organization with an owner and two other active members, one of whom already has administrator rights
criteria.when: the owner grants administrator rights to the second member, that administrator tries to withdraw their own rights, and someone tries to change the owner's
criteria.then: the second member gains administrator rights, and both the self-change and the change to the owner are refused
notes: granting administrator rights requires the person granting them to confirm a statement about what those rights allow before the change is offered.

criteria.statement: Only a service administrator may transfer ownership of an organization, and only to a member whose membership is already active; the previous owner becomes an ordinary member.
criteria.given: an organization with an owner, one active member and one member whose invitation is still pending
criteria.when: an administrator transfers ownership to the active member
criteria.then: that member becomes the organization's owner, the previous owner becomes an ordinary member, and the pending member cannot be chosen as the new owner
notes: the organization's own owner is not offered this action; it is offered only to a service administrator, and only when the organization has at least one member other than the owner.

criteria.statement: The list of an organization's team members can be read only by a service administrator or by someone who owns or administers that organization.
criteria.given: an organization with an owner and one ordinary member
criteria.when: that ordinary member, and separately a vendor unconnected to the organization, asks for the organization's team list
criteria.then: both are refused, while the owner and a service administrator receive the list

criteria.statement: The organizations a vendor may act on behalf of are those they own and those they administer, excluding any that have been archived.
criteria.given: a vendor who owns one organization, administers a second, is an ordinary member of a third, and owns a fourth that has been archived
criteria.when: they ask for the organizations they can act for
criteria.then: the first two are returned and the third and fourth are not

criteria.statement: Asking for the organizations one may act on behalf of as anyone other than a vendor returns an empty list rather than being refused.
criteria.given: a signed-in member of public sector staff, and a visitor who is not signed in
criteria.when: each asks for the organizations they may act on behalf of
criteria.then: each receives an empty list and neither is told they are not permitted
notes: the permission rule for this request is written but never applied — the check tests that the rule exists rather than running it — so nothing is refused here. No harm follows, because the underlying lookup returns nothing for anyone who is not a vendor, but the outcome is an empty success where a refusal was intended. No corrected criterion has been written because it has not been decided whether the new system should refuse or should keep answering with an empty list.
superseded by R-3.20

criteria.statement: An invitation may name the invited person as an ordinary member or as an owner, and any other membership type is rejected.
criteria.given: an organization whose owner is inviting a team member
criteria.when: the invitation names a membership type other than member or owner
criteria.then: the invitation is refused as an invalid membership type
notes: administrator rights are never granted by an invitation; they are granted afterwards to a member who has already joined, as in R-3.12. In practice the team page always sends "member".

criteria.statement: The Edit and Archive controls on an organization's management page are offered only to a person permitted to use them — the organization's owner or a service administrator; an organization administrator who is not the owner sees the organization's profile as read-only, with no Edit and no Archive control, and the service continues to refuse a profile change or an archive request from anyone other than the owner or a service administrator.
A change to an organization's contact phone number made while editing its profile is saved along with every other profile field, and clearing the field removes the stored number.
Asking for the organizations one may act on behalf of is refused as not permitted for anyone who is not a signed-in vendor, rather than answered with an empty list.

In the organization list, the owner's name, the team size and both qualification marks are shown only to a service administrator and, for a given organization, to the vendors who own or administer it; every other viewer sees that organization's legal name, logo, active state and service areas alone, and the owner and qualification columns are not offered at all to a visitor who is not signed in or to public sector staff.
criteria.given: an organization owned by one vendor
criteria.when: a different vendor, who is neither its owner nor one of its administrators, opens the organization list
criteria.then: that organization's row shows its legal name only, with no owner, no team size and no qualification marks, while the same row shown to an administrator carries all of them
notes: the owner and qualification columns are hidden entirely from a visitor who is not signed in and from public sector staff, so only vendors and administrators ever see them.

criteria.statement: Registering an organization requires a legal name, street address, city, region, mail code, country and contact name, each between one and one hundred characters, together with a contact email in a valid email format and of any length; a website address, second address line, contact title and contact phone number may be left out, but each is rejected if given in an invalid format, with the second address line and contact title also limited to one hundred characters.
criteria.given: a signed-in vendor filling in the organization registration form
criteria.when: they submit it with the legal name left blank, or with a contact email of "not-an-email"
criteria.then: the organization is not created and the offending field is reported as invalid, while the same submission with the optional website, second address line, contact title and phone left empty succeeds
notes: the published interface description lists the same set of fields but says nothing about which are required or how long they may be, so the required/optional split and the hundred-character limit rest on the code alone.

criteria.statement: The vendor who registers an organization becomes its owner immediately, and the organization is active from the moment it is registered.
criteria.given: a signed-in vendor with no organizations
criteria.when: they register a new organization
criteria.then: the organization appears under their owned organizations with them recorded as its owner and its team counted as one member, and they are taken to that organization's management page

criteria.statement: When an administrator archives an organization they do not own, its owner is told by email that the organization has been archived.
criteria.given: an active organization owned by a vendor
criteria.when: an administrator archives it
criteria.then: the owner receives a message telling them their organization has been archived by an administrator and that they can no longer use it, and no such message is sent when the owner archives their own organization

criteria.statement: An organization is qualified for Sprint With Us once it has at least two active team members, those members between them hold every capability the service recognises, and its Sprint With Us terms have been accepted.
criteria.given: an organization with an owner and one further active member who between them hold every capability, and whose Sprint With Us terms have not yet been accepted
criteria.when: the owner opens the organization's Sprint With Us qualification page
criteria.then: the team-size and capability requirements are shown as met, the terms requirement as unmet, and the organization is marked as not qualified
notes: only active members count towards the capability total; a member who has been invited but has not yet accepted is excluded.

criteria.statement: An organization is qualified for Team With Us once it has been approved for at least one service area and its Team With Us terms have been accepted.
criteria.given: an organization approved for one service area whose Team With Us terms have not been accepted
criteria.when: the owner opens the organization's Team With Us qualification page
criteria.then: the service-area requirement is shown as met, the terms requirement as unmet, and the organization is marked as not qualified
notes: the database description carried by the old application does not list the Team With Us terms field, the service-area approvals or the membership-rights history at all, so it is behind the schema the application actually uses.

criteria.statement: Accepting an organization's Sprint With Us or Team With Us terms records the date of acceptance, and a second attempt to accept the same terms for the same organization is refused.
criteria.given: an organization whose Sprint With Us terms have not been accepted
criteria.when: its owner reads the terms and accepts them, and then tries to accept them again
criteria.then: the first acceptance is recorded with its date and shown on the qualification page, and the second is refused with a message saying the terms have already been accepted
notes: an administrator reading the terms page is not offered the accept control, so acceptance is in practice an act of the organization's own people.

criteria.statement: Only an administrator may set which service areas an organization is approved for, and saving a selection replaces the organization's previous approvals entirely.
criteria.given: an organization approved for two service areas
criteria.when: an administrator edits the service areas, leaves one of the two ticked, ticks a third, and saves
criteria.then: the organization is approved for exactly the two areas that were ticked and no longer for the one that was cleared, and the same page offers no editing control to the organization's own owner

criteria.statement: An invited person is told by email that the organization has asked them to join, and is offered a way to accept or decline from that message.
criteria.given: a registered vendor who is not a member of a given organization
criteria.when: that organization invites them
criteria.then: they receive a message naming the organization and offering an accept and a decline choice, and following either choice opens their own organizations page with that decision ready to confirm
notes: superseded by R-3.35

criteria.statement: Inviting an email address that belongs to nobody registered with the service creates no membership; the address is instead sent an invitation to register, and the inviter is told the person was not registered but has been notified.
criteria.given: an organization whose owner is inviting team members
criteria.when: they invite an email address that no registered account uses
criteria.then: no pending membership appears on the team list, the address receives an invitation to register with the service, and the owner is shown a warning naming that address

criteria.statement: When a person accepts an invitation, the organization's owner is told they have joined and the new member is told they may now be put forward on the organization's proposals.
criteria.given: a person with a pending invitation to an organization
criteria.when: they accept it
criteria.then: the organization's owner receives a message saying the person approved the request, and the person receives a message saying they have joined the organization's team

criteria.statement: When an invited person declines an invitation rather than accepting it, the organization's owner is told the request was rejected.
criteria.given: a person with a pending invitation to an organization
criteria.when: they decline it
criteria.then: the pending membership is gone from the organization's team list and the owner receives a message saying the person rejected the team request
notes: no message is sent when the organization's own owner or administrator withdraws a pending invitation, nor when an established member leaves; the code that would tell the owner about a member leaving is present but nothing invokes it.

criteria.statement: An organization keeps a changelog of every grant and withdrawal of administrator rights and every transfer of ownership, showing what happened, to whom, when and by whom, most recent first.
criteria.given: an organization whose owner has granted administrator rights to a member and then withdrawn them
criteria.when: the owner opens the organization's changelog
criteria.then: two entries are shown, "Admin Rights Removed" above "Admin Rights Given", each naming the member it concerns, the time it happened and the person who made the change

criteria.statement: An organization's summary of team capabilities counts only members who have accepted their invitation.
criteria.given: an organization whose only member holding a given capability has been invited but has not yet accepted
criteria.when: the owner opens the organization's team page
criteria.then: that capability is shown as one the team does not have, and it becomes shown as held once the invitation is accepted

criteria.statement: The accept and the decline choice offered in an invitation email both open the invited person's own organizations page with the matching confirmation ready, so a person can decline from the message as readily as they can accept.
Only a signed-in vendor who has accepted the service's terms at some point may start a proposal; a request from public sector staff, an administrator or an anonymous visitor is refused.
criteria.given: a visitor who is not signed in, or is signed in as public sector staff or as an administrator
criteria.when: they attempt to start a proposal against a published opportunity
criteria.then: the request is refused and no proposal is created
notes: a vendor who has never accepted the terms is refused as well, so accepting the terms is a precondition of bidding at all, not only of submitting.

criteria.statement: A vendor may hold at most one proposal per opportunity, and a second attempt is refused with a message saying they already have one.
criteria.given: a vendor who already has a proposal, in any state, against a published opportunity
criteria.when: they start a second proposal against the same opportunity
criteria.then: the request is refused with "You already have a proposal for this opportunity." and no second proposal is created

criteria.statement: Submitting a proposal requires the vendor to accept both the program's terms and the service's current terms, and the act of submitting records that acceptance.
criteria.given: a vendor with a complete proposal whose acceptance of the current terms has been reset
criteria.when: they submit the proposal without ticking both the program terms and the service terms
criteria.then: the submit action is unavailable, and a submission that reaches the service anyway is refused

criteria.statement: Only a draft proposal can be deleted, and deleting it removes it permanently.
criteria.given: a proposal that has been submitted
criteria.when: its author asks for it to be deleted
criteria.then: the request is refused, whereas deleting a draft succeeds and the proposal can no longer be opened

criteria.statement: When an opportunity closes, every proposal submitted against it moves to the first review stage of that program and is given an anonymous proponent name numbered from one.
criteria.given: a Sprint With Us or Team With Us opportunity carrying three submitted proposals and one draft
criteria.when: its proposal deadline passes and the opportunity closes
criteria.then: the three submitted proposals move to review of the opportunity's questions and are named "Proponent 1", "Proponent 2" and "Proponent 3", and the draft is left alone
notes: the numbering follows the order the proposals happen to be read in, so it is stable once assigned but not meaningful in itself.

criteria.statement: A vendor cannot see the history of their own Code With Us proposal, although they can see the history of their own Sprint With Us and Team With Us proposals.
criteria.given: a vendor holding one Code With Us proposal and one Sprint With Us proposal, both scored
criteria.when: they open each proposal
criteria.then: the Sprint With Us proposal shows its history and the Code With Us proposal shows none
notes: the three programs otherwise treat history identically, and only the Code With Us rule omits the proposal's own author. Nothing in the code or documents says the omission is deliberate, so a human should rule on whether Code With Us should gain the author or the other two should lose them; no replacement criterion is offered here.
superseded by R-2.9

criteria.statement: A proposal may be created only as a draft or as a submission, in all three programs; any other state is refused.
criteria.given: the published description of the proposal interface
criteria.when: it is compared with what the service accepts
criteria.then: three disagreements appear, and in each the running service is the stricter of the two
notes: the descriptions say a proposal is created as "DRAFT" or "PUBLISHED", but the service accepts only draft or submitted and rejects "PUBLISHED" outright.

the Sprint With Us description lists actions "scoreQuestions", "screenInToCodeChallenge" and "screenOutFromCodeChallenge" that the service no longer accepts; question scoring now happens through the evaluation panel, and the only screening actions are into and out of the team scenario. Team With Us still has a "scoreQuestions" action, so the description is stale rather than wrong in principle.
the descriptions say deleting a proposal requires the opportunity to be in draft; the service requires only that the proposal itself be a draft and does not look at the opportunity at all.

criteria.statement: A Team With Us proposal is accepted however high its proposed cost, even when the hourly rates it names would exhaust the opportunity's budget before the contract ends.
criteria.given: a Team With Us opportunity with a stated maximum budget
criteria.when: a vendor submits a proposal whose hourly rates over the opportunity's working days come to more than that budget
criteria.then: the submission is accepted
notes: the service carries a rule that computes exactly this total and rejects it when it exceeds the budget, but nothing calls that rule on either the create or the edit path. Sprint With Us applies the equivalent ceiling, so the omission looks like an oversight rather than a decision; a human should rule on whether the new system enforces the ceiling. No replacement criterion is offered until that ruling.
superseded by R-2.10

criteria.statement: A vendor may read the history of a proposal they authored, or of a proposal belonging to an organization they own or administer, in all three programs.

A Team With Us proposal is refused when the hourly rates it names, applied at each resource's target allocation across the opportunity's contract period, come to more than the opportunity's maximum budget; the check runs on both the create and the edit path, as the equivalent Sprint With Us check does.
An organization may appear on at most one proposal per opportunity, and a proposal naming an organization that already bid is refused with a pointer to the existing proposal.
criteria.given: an opportunity that already carries a proposal naming a given organization
criteria.when: a different vendor who administers that same organization names it on a new proposal, or an existing proposal is edited to name it
criteria.then: the request is refused with "Please select a different organization." and the identifier of the existing proposal is returned alongside the refusal

criteria.statement: A proposal saved as a draft is accepted however incomplete it is, but its attachments are checked even in draft.
criteria.given: a vendor filling in a new proposal with most fields still blank
criteria.when: they save it as a draft, attaching a file that does not exist
criteria.then: no content validation error is raised for the blank fields, and the save is refused only because of the attachment

criteria.statement: A Code With Us proposal that is not a draft is rejected unless it carries proposal text of 1 to 10,000 characters, additional comments of at most 10,000 characters, and a complete proponent.
criteria.given: a vendor submitting a Code With Us proposal
criteria.when: the proposal text is empty or longer than 10,000 characters, or the additional comments are longer than 10,000 characters
criteria.then: the submission is rejected and the offending field is named in the response

criteria.statement: A Code With Us proponent is either a named individual carrying a legal name, an email address and a full postal address, each field validated in turn, or an organization identified by id and checked only for existence and active status, since the service does not verify that the vendor belongs to the organization they name.
criteria.given: a vendor submitting a Code With Us proposal as an individual
criteria.when: the legal name, email address, street address, city, province, postal code or country is missing, or the email address or phone number is malformed
criteria.then: the submission is rejected and each offending field is named in the response

criteria.statement: A proposal cannot move from draft to submitted once the opportunity's proposal deadline has passed, and a Code With Us proposal cannot be created already marked as submitted after that deadline, which is refused with "This opportunity is no longer accepting proposals."; the equivalent guard is absent from Sprint With Us and Team With Us creation, where the only barrier is that a closed opportunity is no longer visible to a vendor.
criteria.given: an opportunity whose proposal deadline has passed
criteria.when: a vendor submits a draft proposal against it, or creates a new proposal already marked as submitted
criteria.then: both requests are refused with "This opportunity is no longer accepting proposals." and the proposal stays in draft or is not created

criteria.statement: A Sprint With Us proposal may only be submitted on behalf of an organization that is a qualified supplier for that program, and the organization is re-checked at the moment of submission.
criteria.given: a draft Sprint With Us proposal naming an organization that has since lost its qualified status
criteria.when: the vendor submits it
criteria.then: the submission is refused, and a proposal naming no organization at all is refused with "An organization must be specified before submitting."

criteria.statement: A Team With Us proposal may only be submitted on behalf of an organization that is a qualified supplier for that program and that provides every service area the opportunity's resources call for.
criteria.given: a Team With Us opportunity calling for a service area the vendor's organization does not provide
criteria.when: the vendor submits a proposal naming that organization
criteria.then: the submission is refused with "The selected organization does not satisfy this opportunity's service areas."

criteria.statement: Every person named on a proposal's team must be an active member of the organization the proposal is submitted for, refused with "User is not an active member of the organization.", and a Team With Us proposal additionally refuses the same person named twice with "Please select unique team members.", while a Sprint With Us phase applies no such uniqueness check.
criteria.given: a proposal naming a person whose membership of the organization is pending, inactive or absent
criteria.when: the vendor submits it
criteria.then: the submission is refused with "User is not an active member of the organization.", and naming the same person twice is refused with "Please select unique team members."
notes: a team member whose membership is still pending is shown as pending on the proposal rather than being hidden, so a vendor can see why the submission is blocked.

criteria.statement: A Sprint With Us proposal must offer a team for every phase the opportunity requires and no phase it does not, name no more than one scrum master in each phase, cover every capability the opportunity requires across its phases, and stay within each phase's budget and the opportunity's total budget.
criteria.given: a Sprint With Us opportunity with an inception phase and a set of required capabilities
criteria.when: a vendor submits a proposal that omits the inception phase, names two scrum masters, leaves a required capability uncovered, or proposes a total cost above the opportunity's maximum budget
criteria.then: each of those submissions is refused, naming the phase, the team or the cost as the reason

criteria.statement: A Team With Us proposal must name at least one team member, each with an hourly rate of at least one dollar and each against a resource that exists, though the service does not check that the resource belongs to the opportunity being bid on.
criteria.given: a Team With Us opportunity listing one or more resources
criteria.when: a vendor submits a proposal with no team members, with an hourly rate below one dollar, or naming a resource the opportunity does not list
criteria.then: the submission is refused and the member, the rate or the resource is named as the reason

criteria.statement: A response to an opportunity question is rejected if it is empty or longer than the word limit that question carries, or if it answers a question the opportunity does not ask.
criteria.given: an opportunity question carrying a word limit
criteria.when: a vendor submits a response that is empty, that exceeds the word limit, or that is numbered against no question of the opportunity
criteria.then: the submission is rejected with "No matching opportunity question." or with the word-limit error against that response

criteria.statement: Once a proposal has been submitted, the organization it was submitted for cannot be changed until it is withdrawn.
criteria.given: a submitted Sprint With Us or Team With Us proposal
criteria.when: the vendor edits it and names a different organization
criteria.then: the edit is refused with "Organization cannot be changed once the proposal has been submitted", while the same edit on a draft or withdrawn proposal is accepted

criteria.statement: A vendor may withdraw a submitted proposal at any time, and may put a withdrawn proposal back in only while the opportunity is still accepting proposals.
criteria.given: a submitted proposal on an opportunity whose deadline has passed
criteria.when: the vendor withdraws it, and then tries to submit it again
criteria.then: the withdrawal is accepted and the re-submission is refused, whereas before the deadline both are accepted

criteria.statement: A vendor sees only the proposals they authored, plus the proposals of organizations they own or administer, and never another vendor's proposal.
criteria.given: two vendors who each hold a proposal against the same opportunity
criteria.when: each lists their proposals and each opens the other's proposal directly
criteria.then: each list shows only that vendor's own proposal, an organization owner additionally sees their organization's proposals under a separate heading, and opening the other vendor's proposal is refused

criteria.statement: Public sector staff and administrators cannot see any proposal against an opportunity until that opportunity has closed, and never see drafts or unsubmitted proposals.
criteria.given: a published opportunity whose deadline has not yet passed and which carries both draft and submitted proposals
criteria.when: the opportunity's author or an administrator lists its proposals
criteria.then: the request is refused, and once the opportunity has closed the list shows the submitted proposals but never the drafts
notes: a withdrawn proposal is visible to administrators but hidden from the opportunity's own author.

criteria.statement: A Code With Us proposal is scored once out of 100 to two decimal places, and entering that score moves the proposal from review to evaluated.
criteria.given: a Code With Us proposal under review
criteria.when: the opportunity's author enters a score of 87
criteria.then: the proposal becomes evaluated, its history records that a score of "87%" was entered, and a score above 100, below zero or with more than two decimal places is refused

criteria.statement: When every proposal still in contention on an opportunity has been evaluated, the opportunity moves to processing on its own.
criteria.given: an opportunity in evaluation with two proposals under review and one already disqualified
criteria.when: the last of the two is scored
criteria.then: the opportunity moves to processing with the note "Automatically moved to Processing as all proposals have been evaluated.", and disqualified, withdrawn and draft proposals are not counted

criteria.statement: Sprint With Us and Team With Us proposals advance through the evaluation stages one at a time, and an action taken at the wrong stage of the opportunity is refused.
criteria.given: a Sprint With Us opportunity still in its code challenge stage
criteria.when: someone enters a team scenario score for one of its proposals
criteria.then: the request is refused with "The opportunity is not in the correct stage of evaluation to perform that action."

criteria.statement: After the questions of a Sprint With Us or Team With Us opportunity have been scored, only proposals meeting every question's minimum score are ranked by that score and the highest few are carried into the next stage.
criteria.given: a Sprint With Us opportunity with six proposals scored on its questions, one of them below a question's minimum score
criteria.when: the panel's agreed scores are finalised
criteria.then: the proposal below the minimum is left behind, the remaining five are ranked by their question score and the top four move to the code challenge, while on a Team With Us opportunity the top three move to the challenge

criteria.statement: A proposal's price score is its share of the lowest bid among the proposals still in contention, expressed as a percentage, and it is calculated when the last human-entered score is recorded.
criteria.given: two Sprint With Us proposals still in contention, bidding 100,000 and 200,000
criteria.when: a team scenario score is entered for the higher bid
criteria.then: that proposal is given a price score of 50, its history records the calculated price score, and it becomes fully evaluated
notes: a Team With Us bid is the sum of each named person's hourly rate weighted by the target allocation of the resource they are named against, rather than a stated total cost.

criteria.statement: A proposal's total score is the weighted sum of its stage scores, and proposals are ranked against each other only once they are fully evaluated.
criteria.given: an opportunity whose questions, challenge, scenario and price carry stated weights
criteria.when: a proposal has a score for every one of those stages
criteria.then: its total is those scores combined in the stated proportions, and it takes a rank among the other fully evaluated proposals, highest total first

criteria.statement: A vendor sees the scores and rank of their own proposal only after the opportunity has been awarded or their proposal has been passed over.
criteria.given: a vendor's proposal that has been scored but whose opportunity has not been awarded
criteria.when: the vendor opens their proposal
criteria.then: no score and no rank are shown, and both appear once the proposal becomes awarded or not awarded

criteria.statement: Awarding a proposal marks every other proposal still in contention on that opportunity as not awarded and awards the opportunity itself.
criteria.given: an opportunity with one evaluated proposal, one already disqualified and one withdrawn
criteria.when: an administrator awards the evaluated proposal
criteria.then: that proposal becomes awarded, the opportunity becomes awarded, and the disqualified and withdrawn proposals keep the state they were in
notes: only a proposal that is fully evaluated, or one previously passed over, may be awarded.

criteria.statement: A proposal may be disqualified at any stage of evaluation, and doing so requires a written reason of 1 to 5,000 characters.
criteria.given: a proposal at any stage after the opportunity has closed
criteria.when: an administrator disqualifies it without giving a reason
criteria.then: the request is refused, and with a reason given the proposal becomes disqualified, the reason is kept in its history, and the opportunity is re-checked for whether every remaining proposal is now evaluated

criteria.statement: It cannot be determined whether the Sprint With Us stage between reviewing team questions and the code challenge is still reachable.
criteria.given: a Sprint With Us proposal under review on its team questions
criteria.when: it is moved to the stage the running code calls "evaluated questions"
criteria.then: it is not established whether the move succeeds or is rejected
notes: the running code still allows this move and labels the stage with the value "EVALUATED_QUESTIONS", but the migration that introduced the evaluation panel renamed every stored occurrence of that value to "DEPRECATED_EVALUATED_QUESTIONS" and restricted the stored values to a list that no longer contains the old one. No later migration puts it back. On that reading the move would be rejected by the store even though the code offers it. The live path bypasses this stage entirely: finalising the panel's agreed scores moves proposals straight from review of the questions to the code challenge.

The stage between reviewing team questions and the code challenge is deprecated in the old system by its own migration, which comments 'Unused status; deprecate', rewrites every stored occurrence and narrows the permitted values so the old spelling can no longer be stored; only two migrations ever touch that constraint and neither restores it, and the live path moves proposals straight from question review to the code challenge. The new system carries no stage between them.

criteria.statement: Every change of state and every score entered against a proposal is recorded in its history with who did it, when, and any note given.
criteria.given: a proposal that has been submitted, reviewed and scored
criteria.when: someone entitled to see its history opens it
criteria.then: the history lists each state change and each score entry, newest first, each with its author, its time and its note

criteria.statement: Submitting a proposal, awarding one and withdrawing one each send notifications: a confirmation to the submitting vendor, an award notice to the winner and a decision notice to everyone else, and a withdrawal notice to the vendor and to every administrator.
criteria.given: an opportunity with three submitted proposals
criteria.when: one of them is awarded
criteria.then: its vendor receives an award notice and the other two vendors each receive a decision notice, and a later withdrawal sends a notice to the withdrawing vendor and to every administrator

criteria.statement: The address that lists proposals shows nothing but the words "Proposal List".
criteria.given: any visitor, signed in or not
criteria.when: they open the proposals list address
criteria.then: a page appears carrying only the words "Proposal List" and no proposals at all
notes: the page is a stub that was never finished; the working place to see one's proposals is the vendor's dashboard, which lists their own proposals and their organizations' proposals under two headings. Nothing should carry this address forward without a decision about what belongs on it.

An address that renders nothing but the words 'Proposal List' is an unfinished stub rather than behaviour to carry forward. A vendor reaches their own and their organizations' proposals from the dashboard, which R-2.24 already states; the proposal-list-stub entry in spec/contract/surface.yaml is removed with it.

criteria.statement: Anyone entitled to read a proposal can take away a printable copy of it, and staff reading a Sprint With Us or Team With Us copy see the anonymous proponent name until the proposal reaches the challenge stage.
criteria.given: a Sprint With Us proposal under review on its team questions
criteria.when: the opportunity's author opens its printable copy, and then the vendor who wrote it opens the same copy
criteria.then: the staff copy names the proponent only as "Proponent 1" while the vendor's own copy names the organization, and once the proposal reaches the code challenge the staff copy names the organization too

criteria.statement: Only public sector staff and administrators may take away every proposal of an opportunity in one document, and they choose whether that document names the proponents.
criteria.given: a closed opportunity carrying several submitted proposals
criteria.when: a vendor opens the address that exports all of them, and then the opportunity's author opens it
criteria.then: the vendor is refused, the author receives every proposal they are entitled to see in one document, and the author can ask for the same document with the proponents named anonymously
